rules.why: The field is a native <textarea>: the browser gives it the keyboard, the value and the announcement.
A <label for> names the field; clicking it focuses the field.
With a visible label, aria-label makes what is read differ from what is seen.
A field in error points to its message, and the message has text - the color alone says nothing.
Every id in aria-describedby exists, or the help text is never read.
The counter is announced politely only near the limit; aria-live must be present for the script to switch.

manual.why: rows is 3 or more: 96px is three lines, and fewer reads as an Input.
An empty read-only field shows "—" as the content.
